purpose: Latanoprost is used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is commonly prescribed for a condition called glaucoma or high eye pressure (ocular hypertension). Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision and prevent damage to your optic nerve.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes and drains a fluid that keeps it healthy. In glaucoma, this fluid does not drain well enough, causing pressure to build up. Latanoprost works by opening up the drainage channels in your eye so that fluid can flow out more easily, which lowers the pressure.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a gradual change in eye color — your iris (the colored part of your eye) may slowly become more brown over time. Your eyelashes may also grow longer, thicker, or darker. You might notice mild eye redness, stinging, or blurred vision right after using the drop. Some people experience a feeling of something in their eye.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you wear contact lenses — you should remove them before putting in the drop and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Let your doctor know if you have had eye surgery, eye infections, or any inflammation in your eye. If you use other eye drops, wait about 5 minutes between each one. Do not touch the tip of the bottle to your eye or any surface to keep it germ-free. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes once every evening. Use it at the same time each night for best results. Using it more than once a day can actually make it work less effectively, so stick to the once-daily schedule your doctor prescribed.
